Telescope 4.2 gives the phone app the same look as the desktop and shows a running stream as a Live Update on newer Android.

## New

**Phone app in the 4.0 style.** The phone app now looks like the desktop, with coloured cards, the desktop's icons and its switches. The status card spells out where the stream is going and at what quality, for example "To LUNA-PC over USB" and "At 1080p 30 fps". Only the three newest paired computers are listed (the rest are behind **Show all**) and there's a **Remove all** button for when the list gets long.

**Live Update.** On Android 16 and newer a running stream shows as a Live Update, a chip in the status bar that says Streaming. Tapping it shows where the stream goes and a **Stop streaming** button without opening the app.

**720p when the phone gets very hot.** At Android's critical heat level the phone now drops to 720p on top of the 15 fps it already dropped to. The desktop shows "The phone is very hot" while that lasts and the full size comes back once the phone has cooled down for 30 seconds.

## Changed

- Running the desktop from source needs Python 3.12 or newer now (it was 3.11). On Debian 12 that means moving to Debian 13 or installing a newer Python. `start.sh` rebuilds an old Telescope environment automatically once a newer Python is installed.
- The Windows app comes with Python 3.14 and newer versions of the libraries it uses.
- On Android 17 the phone asks for the new Local network permission, which Wi-Fi needs. USB works without it.

## Fixed

- The "Streaming started from your computer" message showed up every time the phone app was opened from its notification instead of only once.
- `start.bat` installs the same library versions as the release builds instead of whatever pip picks.

Update your desktop and phone apps to get the latest release. Found something broken? Open an issue and paste your **Copy diagnostics** report into it.
